response: Yes, corrected QT dispersion (QTcD) can predict left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH) in hypertensive patients. Studies have shown that QTcD is significantly increased in hypertensive patients with LVH compared to those without, and it is strongly correlated with the indices of LVH. A QTcD cut-off value of 60 ms can predict LVH in hypertensive patients with high sensitivity and specificity. This suggests that QTcD can be a useful tool in identifying hypertensive patients at risk of developing LVH.
